title: Second Coming
summary: These passages portray the coming of the Son of Man, resurrection, the gathering of God’s people, Christ’s reign, and renewed creation. Daniel 7 depicts a humanlike figure receiving dominion; Daniel 12 speaks of awakening from death; Matthew 24 describes the Son of Man’s coming and the gathering of the elect. Paul addresses the dead and living at Christ’s coming in 1 Thessalonians and the order of resurrection and reign in 1 Corinthians 15. Revelation 21 turns to the renewed creation. The images belong to different visions and arguments and do not by themselves yield one detailed timetable.
historical_context: The cited settings include Danielic visions, Jesus’ teaching in Matthew, letters addressing Christian hope, and Revelation’s vision. The sources are biblical passages and do not provide separate historical research; the explanation stays with those settings and avoids reconstructing a chronology beyond what the texts state.
canonical_context: Daniel’s vision of dominion and its vision of resurrection are taken up alongside Jesus’ teaching about the Son of Man, Paul’s instruction about resurrection and gathering, and Revelation’s picture of renewal. These passages connect expectation of Christ’s coming with resurrection and the future of creation, while differing in imagery and immediate concern.
literary_context: Daniel and Revelation use apocalyptic visions; Matthew presents teaching in a discourse; 1 Thessalonians offers reassurance about the dead and living; 1 Corinthians argues about resurrection. A vision, a teaching passage, and pastoral or argumentative letters do not function as pieces of a single chronological chart. Their shared hope should be read with their literary forms in view.
covenantal_significance: The passages portray God’s authority over kingdoms and death, the gathering and raising of the faithful, Christ’s reign, and creation’s renewal. Their hope rests in God’s future action, although they describe that future through distinct images and do not settle every question about sequence.
canonical_role: This entry gathers biblical passages about the coming of the Son of Man, resurrection, reign, and renewed creation. It presents their shared hope while preserving differences in genre and emphasis and avoiding an unsupported timetable.

interpretive_notes.note: Read Second Coming in its immediate context before generalizing.
Do not flatten distinct passages into one slogan; let the canon keep its own shape.
